answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake before it may vote, trade, or vouch for another agent, while recording endorsements in a reputation graph. If a cluster of identities coordinates fraud, challenge proofs expose their shared behavior and the protocol slashes their stakes and removes their endorsements. Creating a new identity then requires fresh capital, so a sybil attacker must repeatedly fund disposable agents; falcon, gale, and harbor can remain honest participants without paying that cost.
